items.title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
items.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

items.title: Performance of AI Chatbots in Adult Reconstruction Education: A Comparative Evaluation Using AAOS ResStudy Questions.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly incorporated into orthopedic education, yet their ability to handle complex, clinically oriented questions remains unclear. This study evaluates the accuracy, response time, and citation reliability of contemporary AI chatbots when answering adult reconstruction questions from the AAOS ResStudy question bank. METHODS: Fifty-five multiple-choice adult reconstruction questions were extracted and categorized by anatomic region (hip vs. knee), concept (clinical presentation, prognosis, management), and AAOS-defined difficulty. Seven chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini, Gemini Advanced, Claude, and Co-Pilot) were assessed. Accuracy, response time, and citation quality (existence and relevance) were recorded. Statistical analyses included chi-square testing, t-tests, Pearson correlation, one-way ANOVA, and Kruskal-Wallis testing (p<0.05). RESULTS: Overall chatbot accuracy was 67.5%. GPT-4o performed best (80%), outperforming AAOS members (75%), while Co-Pilot ranked second (70.9%). Accuracy varied by concept, with highest performance in Clinical Presentation (78.6%) and lowest in Prognosis (63.1%). Difficulty strongly influenced performance, with accuracy dropping from 84.7% on very easy questions to 45.4% on difficult ones. Average response time was 3.6 seconds, and no significant correlation existed between speed and accuracy. Among citation-producing chatbots, Co-Pilot achieved 100% citation existence and relevance. CONCLUSION: Modern AI chatbots demonstrate moderate overall accuracy on adult reconstruction questions, with GPT-4o exhibiting the strongest performance. While chatbots excel at descriptive orthopedic knowledge, they continue to struggle with applied reasoning tasks such as prognosis and management. These findings support their use as supplementary, rather than primary, learning tools. Improving citation reliability and reasoning capabilities may enhance future educational applications. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV, Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis.

items.title: Pharmacoeconomic Value of Precision-Guided High-Cost Therapies in Rheumatic and Autoimmune Diseases: A Systematic Review of Cost-Effectiveness, Budget Impact, and Decision Uncertainty
items.abstract: To identify, characterize, and critically appraise comparative economic evaluations and budget impact analyses of precision medicine strategies used to guide the use of high-cost medications for rheumatic and autoimmune diseases. The review will examine strategies based on biomarkers, pharmacogenomics, therapeutic drug monitoring, clinical decision rules, predictive models, machine learning, or artificial intelligence when the resulting information changes a treatment decision. The synthesis will cover incremental costs, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), net monetary benefit, cost savings, budget impact, affordability, value of information, and major sources of uncertainty, with particular attention to the transferability of findings to payers, health technology assessment (HTA) bodies, and public health systems.

items.title: Phytoremediation potential of native plants in fly ash-contaminated sites: a review on heavy metal uptake and soil restoration strategies
items.abstract: Fly ash generated from coal-fired thermal power plants represents one of the largest industrial solid wastes worldwide and poses significant environmental challenges due to its high alkalinity, poor nutrient status, and elevated concentrations of potentially toxic elements such as arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), lead (Pb), nickel (Ni), and mercury (Hg). The uncontrolled disposal of fly ash threatens soil quality, groundwater resources, ecosystem stability, and human health, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable remediation strategies. Among the available technologies, phytoremediation using native plant species has emerged as an environmentally friendly and potentially lower-input because indigenous plants are naturally adapted to local climatic and edaphic conditions, enabling long-term establishment and ecological restoration with minimal external inputs. This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on the physicochemical characteristics of fly ash, heavy metal speciation and bioavailability, and the physiological, biochemical, molecular, and rhizosphere-mediated mechanisms governing heavy metal uptake, translocation, detoxification, and sequestration in native plant species. Unlike previous reviews that primarily provide descriptive accounts of phytoremediation, this review integrates plant functional traits, rhizosphere interactions, soil microbial dynamics, and ecosystem restoration processes into a comprehensive framework for selecting suitable native species for fly ash rehabilitation. The review further discusses recent advances in microbiome-assisted phytoremediation, biochar-assisted remediation, omics technologies, artificial intelligence-assisted species selection, remote sensing, and ecological risk assessment as emerging tools for improving remediation efficiency and long-term restoration monitoring. Existing knowledge gaps, including limited long-term field validation, biomass disposal challenges, insufficient economic assessment, and the need for standardized evaluation criteria, are critically examined. Finally, the review proposes future research priorities and emphasizes the integration of phytoremediation with sustainable land management and environmental policy to support resilient ecosystem restoration and the long-term rehabilitation of fly ash-contaminated landscapes.

items.title: Precision Social Medicine: Bridging the Gap Between Social Care and Health Systems Integration
items.abstract: Health systems serving children have increasingly invested in social care initiatives, yet these programs frequently demonstrate inconsistent effectiveness and face challenges in sustainability and scalability. Precision social medicine (PSM) offers a framework for addressing this gap by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models to match social care interventions to patients' clinical and social context. This article presents a practical, 3-step approach for operationalizing PSM within health systems serving children. These steps are to (1) codefine precision in social care with patients and frontline staff, (2) translate that definition into an AI/ML-informed strategy for identifying risk and assigning services, and (3) test the approach in workflows before it impacts care. We highlight integrating such a framework using pediatric asthma as a case example, tailored for the pediatric hospitalist managing the transition from hospital to home.

items.title: Predicting AI Performance on Unseen Benchmarks Using a Hierarchical Bayesian Model: PAIEC 2026 Technical Report
items.abstract: This technical report presents the research and development of a hierarchical Bayesian prediction system for the AIMS Predictive AI Evaluation Competition (PAIEC 2026), associated with NeurIPS 2026. The research addresses the problem of predicting the probability that an AI system correctly answers questions from previously unseen benchmarks under limited feedback. The evaluation setting involves making initial predictions without labels and subsequently updating predictions as selectively revealed labels become available. Methodology and Technical Contributions • Developed a compact hierarchical Bayesian prediction model incorporating benchmark-level offsets with heavy-tailed priors, pair-level ability, item difficulty pooled across subjects, and item-group effects. • Implemented exact posterior integration and Bayesian pooling to support prediction under sparse feedback and previously unseen benchmark conditions. • Designed a systematic experimental framework incorporating baseline comparisons, leave-one-benchmark-out (LOBO) evaluation, calibration analysis, leakage forensics, signal decomposition, and adversarial red-team experiments. • Established preregistered experiments, explicit statistical decision rules, reproducibility checks, automated validation, and competition submission pipelines. • Implemented the final prediction system using Python and NumPy. Selected Experimental Results • Local leave-one-benchmark-out evaluation (one subject per benchmark, 10 paired seeds): achieved a Brier ALC of 0.2088, compared with 0.2451 for the official baseline. • Official formative evaluation: achieved a mean Brier ALC of 0.1839 across four runs (standard deviation: 0.024). Lower Brier ALC indicates better performance. The local LOBO evaluation and official formative evaluation represent distinct experimental settings and should not be interpreted as a final competition ranking. Reproducibility and Research Artifacts The accompanying repository provides model implementations, experimental scripts, evaluation utilities, automated tests, competition submission artifacts, a technical report, and instructions for reproducing the reported results. The underlying gated measurement dataset is not redistributed and requires separate access. items.title: Predicting East Africa’s rainfall extremes with calibrated AI post-processing systems
items.abstract: Abstract Accurate and reliable rainfall forecasts are crucial for Early Warning Systems (EWS). Artificial Intelligence approaches, which post-process global physical forecasts, enable low-cost ensemble generation, extending skill to medium-range lead times and offering scalable systems to inform EWS particularly under resource-constrained settings. However, assessing their practical value in representing user-relevant rainfall extremes and guiding decisions for EWS remains critical. We present a low-cost, uncertainty quantification method that calibrates ensemble forecasts to probabilities of exceedances for rainfall extremes. Applied to raw and post-processed rainfall forecasts over East Africa, sub-regional analysis shows the threshold-calibrated, post-processed forecasts better reflecting the observed chances of extremes at higher rainfall thresholds. Case-study results show encouraging added value from post-processed forecasts at longer lead times. Forecast skill decomposed across rainfall and probability thresholds highlights the ranges of rainfall and risk tolerances where most actionable improvement arises, whether using satellite or rain-gauge data as reference. This tailored evaluation helps guide forecast adoption for EWS.

items.title: Predicting Motion Sickness Sensitivity
items.abstract: Objective To determine the combined effectiveness of personal factors in predicting motion sickness sensitivity elicited by linear motion of a sled. Background Technologies that create challenging motion environments have spurred the development of mathematical models aimed at predicting motion sickness. Including personal factors may improve their predictive accuracy. History of motion sickness, age, gender, and visual dependence have been identified as potential predictors, although their individual predictive value is limited. Method We assessed motion sickness history, age, and gender through a questionnaire. To evaluate visual dependence, participants oriented a virtual rod parallel to the orientation of gravity while observing a tilted static frame or a disc rotating in roll. Sensitivity is expressed using a new measure that considers both the magnitude and accumulation of self-reported symptoms. Results Our results confirmed the predictive value of history and showed a small yet significant contribution of dynamic visual dependence, with greater dependence associated with higher sensitivity ( R 2 = 25%). Recent history reported over the past 10 years was demonstrated as a better predictor than lifetime history. Age, gender, and static visual dependence did not enhance the prediction. Conclusion Combining multiple predictors shows little advantage for improving a prediction of sensitivity beyond history alone. Future studies could confirm the predictive value of dynamic visual dependence and seek to optimize recent history, for example, by restricting time period and motion environment. Application Improved prediction models may support tailoring system parameters to user sensitivity in technologies such as automated driving, head mounted displays, and simulators.

items.title: Premolar extraction versus non-extraction orthodontic treatment: an AI-assisted systematic review and meta-analysis of all reported outcomes with GRADE assessment (retrospective registration)
items.abstract: RETROSPECTIVE REGISTRATION. This registers the protocol (version 1.0, fixed 25 October 2026) of a systematic review comparing comprehensive orthodontic treatment with premolar extraction against comprehensive treatment without extraction, for every reported effectiveness and adverse-effect outcome. The protocol was fixed before screening but was not registered before screening began; this registration was made on 2 November 2026, after searching, screening, data extraction and analysis had been completed. All differences between the protocol and the completed review are reported in the manuscript (Table of protocol deviations). Purpose: to provide one review covering all premolar-extraction patterns and all outcomes (occlusion, treatment duration, soft-tissue profile, incisor and molar position, skeletal and vertical change, arch dimensions, smile, stability, root resorption, periodontal, airway, temporomandibular, patient-reported and third-molar outcomes), with risk of bias (RoB 2, ROBINS-I), random-effects meta-analysis, prediction intervals and GRADE certainty ratings, and an explicit comparison with earlier systematic reviews. The review was run as an AI-agent workflow under the supervision of the human guarantor (Prof Ahmed Elkhadem, Faculty of Dentistry, Cairo University).

items.title: Professional choice motivation and flow experience in specialized skill courses: a three-way interaction analysis among undergraduate physical education majors
items.abstract: Specialized skill courses are a crucial component of talent cultivation in physical education programs. However, their long duration and high intensity often lead to declines in student engagement, thereby affecting skill acquisition. Flow experience, as a key psychological indicator of learning states, can effectively reflect students’ actual level of involvement. Focusing on professional choice motivation, this study examined its relationship with flow experience in specialized skill courses among undergraduate physical education majors and further tested the three-way interaction among professional choice motivation, physical self-efficacy, and physical activity volume. Using the Professional Choice Motivation Scale, Physical Self-Efficacy Scale, Physical Activity Rating Scale, and the absorption subscale of the Flow Short Scale, data were collected on two survey occasions 3 months apart. A total of 398 valid responses were obtained at T1, and 203 valid responses were obtained when the T1 participants were surveyed again at T2. Because individual responses could not be matched across the two occasions, the two datasets were analyzed separately. Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, three-way interaction analysis, and conditional effect tests were performed using R. The results showed that both intrinsic motivation ( β T1 = 0.72, β T2 = 0.64, p T1T2 < 0.001) and extrinsic motivation ( β T1 = 0.61, β T2 = 0.53, p T1T2 < 0.001) were significantly and positively associated with flow experience at both survey occasions. Furthermore, the three-way interaction among professional choice motivation, physical self-efficacy, and physical activity volume was significant at both T1 and T2 and showed the same negative direction ( p T1T2 < 0.05). Conditional effect tests showed that, except for the high physical activity volume/high physical self-efficacy condition at T2, intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation were significantly and positively associated with flow experience under all other conditions. These findings contribute to a more contextualized understanding of the relationship between professional choice motivation and flow experience and offer important theoretical implications for instructional practice in specialized skill courses.

items.title: Prompt style effects on large language model differential diagnosis output in adolescent catatonia and psychosis
items.abstract: Prompt engineering shapes large language model (LLM) output, but practicing clinicians have little guidance on which prompting style suits a given clinical task. A single publicly available, de-identified pediatric psychiatric case report was submitted to a base, unauthenticated ChatGPT-5.5 session under four prompt conditions: zero-shot, chain-of-thought, role/persona, and structured/constrained output. Each output was scored from 0 (feature absent) to 2 (complete) on four criteria: diagnostic accuracy, causative agent recognition, safety completeness, and calibration. Output was compared against the published clinical course. Total scores were zero-shot 7/8, chain-of-thought 6/8, role-persona 7/8, and structured 7/8. All four conditions ranked bipolar I disorder above substance-induced psychotic disorder, whereas the treating team's documented differential favored unspecified and substance-induced categories without a confirmed bipolar diagnosis. All four conditions recommended neuroimaging, electroencephalography, and lumbar puncture, exceeding the workup the treating team actually performed. Across four prompt styles, core diagnostic content was materially the same; the styles differed in the precision of probability quantification and in reasoning transparency, not in the underlying differential generated.

items.title: Prompting Metacognition: Using Prompt Writing as a Language Task and Metacognitive Tool in ELT
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools have made their way into English Language Teaching (ELT) contexts, yet their pedagogical value remains contested. While many learners engage with GenAI primarily as a quick hack for producing answers, fewer use it as a resource for reflective language learning. This study explores prompt writing as a language learning task that supports both language development and metacognitive awareness. The study was conducted with a target group of pre-seminary, tertiary-level learners with mixed linguistic proficiency. Over the course of four instructional sessions, the study used a classroom-based action research design. Learners engaged in cycles of prompt drafting, GenAI-generated responses, peer discussion, and prompt refinement. Classroom observations, learner reflections, and group discussions were used to gather qualitative insights. The findings indicate measurable improvement in learners’ autonomy, as learners became aware of how lexical choices shape meaning, along with increased engagement, teamwork, and reflective thinking. The study argues that prompt writing, when treated as a language task rather than a technical skill, can function as a practical tool for fostering metacognition in ELT classrooms.

items.title: Psychosocial Working Conditions in a Portuguese Social Care Institution: A Descriptive Case Study by Occupational Group
items.abstract: Abstract: Psychosocial working conditions have become an increasingly relevant concern in occupational health, particularly in social care contexts where employees are exposed to demanding emotional and physical environments. This study examines the main psychosocial factors affecting workers in a Portuguese private social solidarity institution and explores their implications for well-being and productivity. A descriptive quantitative case study was conducted, supported by a literature review and a questionnaire applied to different professional groups within the organisation. The findings suggest that, although overall levels of psychosocial risk are relatively low, there are meaningful differences across occupational categories. Frontline care workers appear to be the most exposed group, followed by kitchen staff and technical personnel. Across the sample, emotional and physical demands, work pace, task overload and limited recognition emerged as the most significant factors. These results indicate that even in seemingly stable organisational environments, certain roles remain particularly vulnerable to psychosocial strain. The study underscores the importance of adopting preventive and organisational measures to foster healthier, more supportive working conditions, as these are essential for both employee well-being and the quality of care provided. Foi realizado um estudo de caso quantitativo descritivo, apoiado por uma revisão da literatura e por um questionário aplicado a diferentes grupos profissionais dentro da organização. items.title: Public Awareness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Utilisation in Healthcare Institutions in Anambra State
items.abstract: Given the growing adoption of AI-driven diagnostic and treatment tools across health systems, understanding community awareness is crucial for effective integration and health communication. Applying the survey design, data were collected from 384 adult residents selected from across six Local Government Areas of Anambra State, Nigeria, using multistage and proportionate sampling techniques. Findings revealed a moderately high level of awareness of AI utilisation, with respondents expressing the strongest familiarity with AI-powered tools such as automated diagnostics and virtual assistants. Social media emerged as the dominant source of AI information, followed by traditional media, while healthcare providers contributed minimally to public knowledge. Respondents also recognised significant benefits of AI, including improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced service delivery, and overall healthcare quality. However, concerns were evident regarding potential medical errors, privacy concerns, and job displacement of healthcare workers. These findings align with national and international studies showing high exposure but limited depth of understanding among the public and health workers. Guided by the Diffusion of Innovations and Agenda-Setting theories, the study concludes that public awareness is largely media-driven and remains at an early diffusion stage, underscoring the need for deliberate institutional communication, ethical safeguards, and structured public sensitisation. The study recommends strengthening health communication strategies, promoting data protection frameworks, and enhancing healthcare worker involvement in public AI education.

items.title: QbD-Optimized Colon-Targeted Mucoadhesive Tablet for Enhanced Plecanatide Delivery in IBS-C Management
items.abstract: Background: Plecanatide, which is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome constipation (IBS-C), is highly susceptible to gastric enzymatic degradation, impairing critical therapeutic efficacy and bioavailability. This work designed an improved site-directing, colon-targeted mucoadhesive formulation to guarantee site-specific delivery and efficacy. Methods: Design-Expert software 13 was used in a systematic optimization system with different concentrations of Na-alginate, Carbopol 934, and Methocel K15M. Flowability and compressibility were evaluated by pre-compression analysis. To specifically target the distal colon, the in vitro dissolution kinetics and cellular activity against the HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells were assessed. They were in vivo studies that measured mucosal recovery, submucosal pathology, and systemic oxidative stress biomarkers (MDA and SOD). In the accelerated stability testing, the standardized periods were tested under controlled laboratory conditions. Results: Methocel K15M proved to be the best polymer. The formulation exhibited 24 h sustained release, which fit best in the Hixson–Crowell (r = 0.980) and Higuchi (r = 0.956) models. Cellular activity against the HCT116 cells was high (IC50 = 79.31 ug/mL), being ten-fold better than the raw API. In vivo, the mucoadhesive system demonstrated almost total inflammatory resolution of all the layers of the colon. As opposed to regular tablets, it had a tremendous impact in reducing MDA (p = 0.014) and raising the activity of SOD (p = 0.002). Accelerated stability testing (40 °C/75% RH for 6 months) showed a slight decrease in drug content from 100.85% to 96.78%, which remained within the acceptable pharmacopeial limits (90–110%), confirming formulation stability. Conclusions: The mucoadhesive Plecanatide formulation is a “site-directing colon-targeted mucoadhesive formulation” that can effectively overcome the shortcomings of traditional therapy; i.e., it exhibits the potential for better compliance. This formulation mitigates inflammatory and oxidative stress, offering a stable, promising alternative for managing chronic IBS-C symptoms and enhancing patient health outcomes in contemporary clinical practice and pharmaceutical standards.

items.title: QSAR-guided generative framework for the discovery of synthetically viable odorants
items.abstract: Abstract The discovery of novel odorant molecules is key for the fragrance and flavor industries, yet efficiently navigating the vast chemical space to identify structures with desirable olfactory properties remains a significant challenge. Generative artificial intelligence offers a promising approach for de novo molecular design but typically requires large sets of molecules to learn from. To address this problem, we present a framework combining a variational autoencoder (VAE) with a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) model to generate novel odorants from limited training sets of odor molecules. The self-supervised learning capabilities of the VAE allow it to learn SMILES grammar from ChemBL database, while its training objective is augmented with a loss term derived from an external QSAR model to structure the latent representation according to odor probability. While the VAE demonstrated high internal consistency in learning the QSAR supervision signal, validation against an external, unseen ground truth dataset (Unique Good Scents) confirms the model generates syntactically valid structures (100% validity achieved via rejection sampling) and 94.8% unique structures. The latent space is effectively structured by odor likelihood, evidenced by a Frechet ChemNet Distance (FCD) of ≈ 6.96 between generated molecules and known odorants, compared to ≈ 21.6 for the ChemBL baseline. Structural analysis via Bemis-Murcko scaffolds reveals that 74.4% of candidates possess novel core frameworks distinct from the training data, indicating the model performs extensive chemical space exploration beyond simple derivatization of known odorants. Generated candidates display physicochemical properties consistent with ground-truth odorants (mean MW ∼158 Da, LogP ∼1.67) and comparable predicted ADMET profiles. Furthermore, quantum mechanical calculations (GFN2-xTB) verify thermodynamic stability with energy distributions matching known volatiles, and automated retrosynthesis demonstrates practical viability, yielding valid synthesis routes for 100% of candidates, averaging 2.89 steps from commercially available precursors. This integrated approach provides a novel and systematic methodology for applying generative AI to explore chemical space specifically for the discovery of new candidate odorant molecules.

items.title: Qualitative Study on the Role of AI-Driven Problem Based Learning in Transforming Biology Classroom for Dual Mandate System in Nigeria
items.abstract: Dual mandate - the federal College of Education act 2023 signed by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu legally and officially empowered these institutions to award education degrees while the NCE programmes continues. The Nigerian curriculum for biology at the senior secondary school level is designed to help students develop a range of skills which include understanding biological concepts and principles, application of the knowledge to solve real-life situations, problem solving skills and ability to communicate biological ideas and concepts effectively. Problem based learning is a pedagogical approach that involves students learning through the experience of solving real world problems. It is a student centered approach that encourages critical and creative thinking, collaboration, active learning and application of skills to solve real world problems. Problem based learning can be effectively integrated with STEM subjects; science, technology, education and mathematics. Problem based learning is grounded in several theories like constructivist, social constructivism posits by Vygotsky 1978. Artificial Intelligence has the potential to make up for the shortcomings of traditional problem based learning by giving full account of students reports in the project, timely feedback and helps teachers to monitor students learning outcome. AI tools used in education/science include machine learning algorithms; natural language processing techniques which are used to create personalized learning; AI powered VR or AR are also used. AI driven PBL used include Khammigo or custom GPT, Google Docs, Padlet AI, Gradescope, Google sheets etc. The global AI in education market size was estimated at USD 5.88 billion in 2024 is projected to grow at Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 31.2% from 2025 to 2030. However, with PBL, the teachers have to provide students with necessary resources e.g. learning materials, tools and technological support as well as guidance. One of the opportunities of integrating AI in education include personalized learning, creating more interactive and immersive learning experiences, games and simulations that boost students confidence, motivation and persistence leading to improved academic achievement.

items.title: Quantifying Threshold Sensitivity in Vision-Based Ergonomic Assessment: Decision Stability of RULA and REBA in a Batik Workshop
items.abstract: Automated pose-estimation pipelines usually report one RULA or REBA score per frame, without indicating whether that decision would survive small errors in the estimated joint angles. Both instruments convert continuous angles into ordinal categories through fixed thresholds and non-additive lookup tables, so the same angular error may leave one decision unchanged while reversing another. Earlier vision-based studies report aggregate agreement with reference systems or experts; none attaches a robustness statement to the individual decision. This study proposes a reproducible protocol that does so. It combines an observability audit, conditional lower and upper bounds for decisions whose inputs cannot all be seen, controlled angle-level perturbation at magnitudes anchored to published single-camera angle errors (σ = 2, 5, 8, and 12°), and a set of metrics in which baseline decision retention (BDR) measures whether the reported decision survives and the Ergonomic Decision Stability Index (EDSI) measures the probability of the most frequent category after perturbation. The protocol was instantiated on one batik worker (four photographs, four videos). At the level of the RULA action level, the four photographed postures retained their lower-bound decision in at least 93% of replications at σ = 5°, although two of them lay only 0.1° and 0.2° from a component threshold, where distance-based predictors anticipated retention of only 21–52%. The same posture that was stable under RULA retained its REBA risk level in only 49% of replications. Unobserved inputs left the final action level undetermined between its bounds for every posture. Across 534 video frames, component-level stability fell from 0.88 at 2° to 0.40 at 12°. The results demonstrate the method on one case; they do not support population inference or a validated triage rule.

items.title: Quantum-inspired annealing-based semantic-aware optimization for sustainable cloud-edge intelligence
items.abstract: The swift development of artificial intelligence (AI) models within cloud-edge systems has intensified energy usage and created sustainability challenges, prompting concerns about sustainable AI. Recent studies have investigated quantum-inspired optimization and resource orchestration to improve efficiency; however, the majority of current approaches regard data samples and model updates as equally significant, overlooking their semantic impact on learning results. This research presents Semantic–Energy Aware Quantum-Inspired Adaptive Learning (SEA-QAL), an optimization methodology addressing semantic relevance, energy consumption, and predictive efficacy in distributed cloud–edge AI frameworks. In contrast to current energy-aware optimization techniques, SEA-QAL directly integrates semantic utility assessment with quadratic interaction-aware decision optimization via a closed-loop sustainability controller. The approach includes a semantic evaluation system that assesses update impact through gradient sensitivity, prediction uncertainty, and attention-driven representational signals. Semantic utility functions as an indicator of learning significance rather than a comprehensive measure of semantic meaning. These indicators are employed in energy cost modelling to develop a loss-energy-semantic Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) framework. The resultant choice problem is addressed with a quantum-inspired annealing method that combines probabilistic state transitions with tunneling-like exploration in a classical computing framework. The approach improves optimization by including semantic utility, reducing unnecessary computation and communication costs while maintaining the model’s generalization capabilities. Comprehensive experiments conducted in cloud-edge workload contexts, including perception-oriented, sensor-based, and IoT-edge evaluations, demonstrate improvements in sustainability indicators, such as reduced energy usage and communication overhead, while achieving comparable or enhanced prediction accuracy relative to benchmarks. Furthermore, the evaluation of scalability with augmented edge-node configurations demonstrates the effectiveness of SEA-QAL for medium-scale cloud-edge deployments.

items.title: Query Suggestion for Text-to-Image Retrieval
items.abstract: The challenge of translating a user's information need into an effective search query is fundamental in modern cross-modal retrieval systems, which allow users to search image collections with natural language but often lack interactive refinement tools. Our paper addresses the gap by investigating Cross-modal Query Suggestion, the task of dynamically generating targeted query alternatives that verbalize the semantic content of visually coherent image groups within an initial retrieval result set. Building upon our prior work establishing a dedicated benchmark, this extended study systematically compares three distinct methodological paradigms for generating these suggestions: i) latent-conditioned generation, which operates on visual embeddings; ii) caption-based generation, relying on textual abstractions of the result set; and iii) image-conditioned generation, which directly utilizes representative images from the result set as input for Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). We further expand the evaluation framework by introducing new metrics for semantic fidelity against human annotations and computational efficiency. While our evaluation assumes a controlled setup with disjoint image clusters, we validate its robustness against automated partitioning and noise. This work establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework to map the structural trade-offs of these paradigms, and validates the effectiveness of the proposed protocol with a tailored user preference study. Our experiments demonstrate that approaches utilizing direct visual grounding via LMMs produce more image-specific suggestions, Large Language Models (LLMs) reach the best tradeoff between the assessed properties, while latent-conditioned methods have the lowest computational cost. These findings offer critical insights for developing dynamic, visually informed interactive search systems. The dataset, the methods implementations and the code to replicate our experiments are available at: github.com/Ruggero1912/CroQS-benchmark

items.title: Radiomics- based biomarkers for immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer: advances, challenges, and future perspectives in biological interpretation and clinical translation
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet treatment benefit remains heterogeneous and resistance is common. Genomic alterations, tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming across spatial and temporal scales that are incompletely captured by single-site tissue sampling. Radiomics extracts quantitative features from routine images and offers a framework for investigating macroscopic correlates of these processes. This narrative review critically examines computed tomography (CT) and fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT (¹ 8 F-FDG PET/CT) radiomics in relation to oncogenic alterations, immune and stromal phenotypes, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, tumor mutational burden, and metabolic–immune interactions in NSCLC. It should be highlighted that such observed statistical links only generate plausible biological hypotheses and do not constitute experimental proof of true mechanistic relationships. Rather than merely summarizing predictive model performance, we emphasize evidence boundaries and interpretive caveats for radiomic-TME associations. We further elaborate on key translational bottlenecks including limited reproducibility, technical standardization deficits, and retrospective-model overfitting. We discuss ongoing efforts toward cross-scale multi-omics integration, alongside the promises and inherent limitations of explainable artificial intelligence and federated learning for clinical translation. To move beyond purely predictive tools toward mechanism-aware decision-support systems, future radiomic research requires prospective multicenter validation, rigorous data harmonization, and combined analyses integrating spatial transcriptomics, digital pathology, and circulating biomarkers for precision immuno-oncology.

items.title: Reading–Writing Integration Through ChatGPT-Supported Feedback: Growth, Associations, and Mediated Pathways of Student Engagement in Chinese Classrooms
items.abstract: Abstract Although reading–writing integration has been increasingly advocated in Chinese language education, limited empirical evidence explains how reading, writing, and student engagement become integrated, particularly under AI-supported feedback. To address this issue, this study examined whether ChatGPT-supported feedback improved reading outcomes, writing outcomes, and student engagement, while investigating their interrelationships, the mediating role of student engagement, and the corresponding pathways in reading–writing integration. A total of 400 middle school students from eight intact classes in Shenzhen participated, with 200 students receiving ChatGPT-supported feedback and 200 receiving human-generated feedback. Using a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design, data were analyzed within a quantitative longitudinal framework integrating baseline equivalence tests, 2 × 2 mixed-design ANOVAs, factor-level correlation analyses, and multi-group cross-lagged path analysis to examine changes and temporal relationships among reading, student engagement, and writing across two groups (N = 400). Despite comparable pretest scores, findings showed that Group 1 demonstrated significantly greater pretest–posttest gains in reading, student engagement, and writing, with significant Time × Group interactions and large effects. Correlations further indicated stronger posttest associations among engagement, reading, and writing in Group 1, whereas these relationships remained weak in Group 2. Longitudinal analyses revealed stronger T2 within-time direct and mediating pathways in Group 1, alongside several significant cross-lagged effects, but cross-lagged mediating effects were generally nonsignificant in both groups. The findings theoretically highlight student engagement as a potentially time-sensitive mechanism through which AI-supported learning may strengthen the integration of reading and writing. Practically, they suggest the pedagogical value of AI-supported learning environments for fostering engagement and connecting literacy processes, while emphasizing sustained instructional exposure to consolidate these relationships over time.

items.title: Real-time geometric complexity of language is associated with global functioning across psychosis and major depression
items.abstract: Abstract Language disturbances are prominent across psychiatric disorders, yet their underlying organization and relationship to clinical functioning remain poorly understood. We conceptualized spontaneous speech as a temporally evolving sequence of contextual representations through semantic space, in which successive concepts define transitions between large-language-model embeddings. We characterized the local dynamics of these representations using Lyapunov-inspired measures of sensitivity to perturbation and anisotropy—the extent to which nearby neighboring contextual representations diverge differently depending on direction in representational space. We applied this approach to picture descriptions from 129 German-speaking participants with major depressive disorder (n = 43), schizophrenia spectrum disorders (n = 42), or no psychiatric diagnosis (n = 44). Individual differences in local geometric dynamics predicted multiple clinical dimensions, with the strongest association observed for global functioning, for which the geometric measures explained 51% of the variance. Clinically informative geometric structure was already detectable within the first three sentences of speech, where distinct dynamical profiles were associated with differences in negative and positive symptoms, anxiety, depression, and global functioning. These associations suggest that the dynamics of local representational divergence and contraction during speech reflect broad variation in cognitive and social functioning rather than diagnosis alone. Together, these findings suggest that psychiatric variation is reflected not simply in what people say, but in the dynamics by which semantic representations evolve during ongoing language production. A dynamical-geometric analysis of language may provide a compact, transdiagnostic marker of clinically meaningful variation in psychopathology.

items.title: Realization and analysis of Artificial Intelligence appearance in Agricultural system
items.abstract: Agriculture is increasingly expected to produce more food while minimizing the usage of water, chemical-based fertilizers, energy, chemicals, and labor. Agricultural decision-making is further complicated by climate unpredictability, soil degradation, shortages of water, crop illnesses, pests, weeds, and yield uncertainties. An IEEE-style review and implementation methodology for AI in agriculture is presented in this research. Examined are a number of important applications, including as crop recommendations, crop-yield estimation, disease and pest recognition, weed identification, soil and nutrient administration, smart irrigating, weather forecasting, livestock monitoring, agricultural robots, and post-harvest management. A multilayer AI-enabled farming system is proposed in which a conventional sensor, image processing, and historical information are acquired through IoT, UAV, satellites, and field devices; processed information is provided to machine-learning(ML)/deep-learning models; and the ensuing decisions are transmitted to farmers or automated actuators. Conventional models such as Decision Tree(DT), Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor(KNN), Support Vector Machine(SVM), and Artificial Neural Network(ANN) are contrasted conceptually with CNN, LSTM, and Transformer-based techniques.Substantial research gaps in dataset variety, model generalization and explanation, efficiency of computation, cybersecurity, field validation,, and cost for small-scale farmers are also identified in the report. For sustainable intelligent agriculture, a future research path based on explainable AI, edge intelligence, hybrid AI, and multimodal data fusion is suggested.

items.title: Reconstructing Core Competencies of Front-Office Employees in South Korean Professional Sports Organizations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Delphi Study
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly reshapes organizational decision-making, fan engagement, and business operations, the competencies expected of front-office employees are also evolving. This study aimed to reconstruct the core competencies required of front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations in the AI era. To this end, a three-round Delphi study was conducted with 20 experts from academia, South Korean professional sports organizations, and research institutes. The Delphi process involved generating competency items, evaluating their relevance, and establishing expert consensus regarding the final competency framework. The findings identified 28 competency items grouped into the following five competency domains: Data & AI Utilization Competency, Human–AI Collaboration Competency, Marketing & Fan Engagement Competency, Communication & Execution Competency, and Ethics & Values Competency. These findings suggest that competencies in AI-enabled professional sports organizations extend beyond technical proficiency and warrant an integrated combination of technological, collaborative, organizational, relational, and ethical capabilities. This study refines the application of competency theory to AI-supported work by providing a context-specific framework for front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations. The proposed framework offers a foundation for understanding how South Korean professional sports organizations may reconstruct workforce competencies in response to the evolving demands of the AI era.

items.title: Regulating AI-Generated Inventions in Tanzania: A Comparative Analysis of BRELA and South Africa’s CIPC
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now produce technical solutions with little or no human contribution to the inventive step, and the DABUS applications filed by Dr Stephen Thaler have tested whether patent law can accommodate an inventor that is not a person. Courts and offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Europe, Australia and Germany have refused, while South Africa’s Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) published the grant of a patent naming DABUS as inventor in July 2021. This article asks whether Tanzania’s Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) could follow that example under the Patents (Registration) Act, Cap 217, and, if not, what reform is required. Using doctrinal analysis and functional comparison, it finds that the two statutes are closer than is usually assumed: neither defines ‘inventor’, and both require an applicant who is not the inventor to show a right derived from the inventor. The decisive difference is administrative. The South African grant followed a formalities-only check in which, on the published record, the applicant’s entitlement was not tested, leaving validity to revocation proceedings. Section 25(7) and (8) of Cap 217, by contrast, require the Registrar to examine every request for compliance with section 18(3) and (4) and to reject one that is not corrected. An application naming DABUS would therefore fail at the formal stage, and one naming a human who did not devise the invention would be open to invalidation under section 64(2)(d). BRELA cannot reproduce the CIPC outcome by discretion. The article recommends, in order of priority, statements of practice on AI-assisted inventions, revised forms, a statutory definition of inventor and, after regional consultation through ARIPO and the East African Community, a deliberate legislative choice on whether AI-generated inventions should be protected.

items.title: Regulatory and scientific frameworks for AI-driven biosensor technologies in antimicrobial resistance monitoring
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) diagnostics require evidence matched to the intended clinical or surveillance use. This narrative review synthesizes biosensor research, artificial intelligence (AI) analytics, and device oversight through a regulatory-scientific lifecycle perspective. Electrochemical and optical transduction are distinguished from microfluidic sample handling and nanomaterial enhancement. Pathogen identification, resistance-gene detection, phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) prediction, and population surveillance are compared by output, reference standard, and validation requirement. Representative Raman-machine-learning and microfluidic studies illustrate both analytical promise and limitations in independent clinical validation. The review maps these findings to US and European device pathways, software controls, interoperability, cybersecurity, and data governance. Its proposed five-phase framework adapts established total-product-lifecycle, quality-management, and risk-management principles to AMR-specific challenges, including emerging resistance mechanisms, breakpoint revisions, specimen shifts, and algorithm changes. The framework is a conceptual implementation tool, not a new regulatory pathway or an empirically validated model. Safe translation requires claim-specific validation and controlled updates rather than extrapolation from isolated prototype performance.

items.title: Relational Differentiation of Normative Possibilities in Epistemic–Praxis Generalized Language Systems
items.abstract: This paper investigates the relational differentiation of future normative possibilities in epistemic–praxis generalized language systems (EP-GLS), where interpretive and justificatory practices interact with consequential action. Its central question concerns institutional histories that yield equivalent present decisions while developing different practical possibilities for subsequent claims, reasons, and responses. Seven deliberately finite comparisons distinguish outcome equivalence, encounter order, typed linkage, pathway robustness, classification refinement, reason-sensitive adoption, and participant-indexed revision. These constructions establish conditional possibility and identification limits. They provide neither evidence of new moral rights nor a general theorem of normativity. The paper develops a layered account of the formation and justification of practical normative relations. An encounter may introduce an interpretive distinction, evidentiary scrutiny may support its use, and competent authorization may make a differentiated response executable. The resulting arrangement can change whose interests are affected and which future objections are practicable. Yet identical participant-indexed responses can arise through direct exchange, centralized computation, or common external direction. Claims about reciprocal co-formation therefore require evidence about communication provenance, participants' actual uptake of reasons, institutional enactment, and subsequent opportunities for criticism. Ethical legitimacy remains a separate question. The proposed research programme reconstructs claim trajectories in linguistic, scientific, governance, and AI-mediated practices while distinguishing interpretive adequacy, causal explanation, and situated normative evaluation. It considers historical inheritance, affected persons outside official records, distributed authority, and plural grounds for judgment. Work in pragmatism, inferentialism, participatory sense-making, conceptual affordances, and sociotechnical co-production provides substantial precedents. The present contribution is narrower: a history-sensitive comparative framework for studying how practical normative possibilities are distributed, transformed, and attributed to encounters. All examples are constructed and the comparative protocols remain prospective; independent empirical validation and comprehensive source-based interpretation remain open.

items.title: REPOSITIONING NIGERIAN POLYTECHNIC CHEMISTRY PROGRAMMES FOR THE FOURTH INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR EMBEDDING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE CURRICULUM
items.abstract: The emergence of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) is fundamentally altering the landscape of the global chemical sector through automation, cyber-physical infrastructures, machine learning, and data-intensive approaches to discovery. These shifts have generated an acute need for professionals who can function effectively at the convergence of chemistry, computation, and digital technologies. In contrast, Nigerian polytechnics (institutions constitutionally tasked with cultivating mid-level technical expertise) continue to operate largely conventional, content-saturated chemistry curricula that show little correspondence with these evolving workforce expectations. This conceptual study set out to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could be systematically woven into the chemistry curricula of Nigerian polytechnics as a means of equipping graduates for Industry 4.0. By triangulating scholarship on AI in education, chemistry pedagogy, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and Industry 4.0 workforce requirements, the paper constructed a conceptual architecture for curriculum integration and evaluated four distinct integration pathways: the supplementary, embedded, dual-track, and fully reformed models. The analysis also interrogated the structural, human-capital, infrastructural, ethical, and policy-related obstacles that impede AI uptake within Nigerian polytechnics, while delineating the Industry 4.0 capabilities that chemistry graduates must command—namely data literacy, computational reasoning, digitally mediated laboratory competence, and AI-supported problem resolution. The study concludes that a staged, context-attuned integration approach—anchored in purposeful policy reform, lecturer capacity building, industry collaboration, and deliberate investment in digital infrastructure—is indispensable for sustaining the relevance of Nigerian polytechnics. Concrete recommendations are advanced for curriculum authorities, institutional managers, and industry stakeholders.

items.title: Research Evolution and Hotspot Detection of AIGC-Empowered Education in China, 2022–2025
items.abstract: With the breakthrough advancement of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AIGC) technology, its integration into education has become a central issue in the global digital transformation of education. To systematically reveal the research status, hotspots, and evolutionary trends in the field of AIGC-empowered education in China, this study draws on the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection. It combines bibliometric and content analyses to examine 1,505 English-language journal articles published by Chinese scholars between 2022 and 2025. The bibliometric results show that publication output in this field has grown explosively since 2022, forming a research landscape centered on highly cited educational-technology journals and characterized by multidisciplinary integration; research hotspots are concentrated on themes such as the educational applications of large language models, instructional innovation, learning outcomes, educational ethics, and intelligent tutoring systems; and the field's development has proceeded through three stages—technology introduction, application exploration, and deep integration—with the research frontier now shifting toward personalized learning, smart-education ecosystems, and digital transformation.

items.title: Research on the application framework of multi-agent technology-driven failure analysis for industrial products
items.abstract: Abstract Accurate failure analysis in intelligent supercharging stations is critical for operational safety and efficiency. However, traditional methods suffer from poor cross-condition adaptability, limited few-shot learning capability, and insufficient cross-model generalization. This paper proposes a Multi-Agent Failure Analysis Execution System (FAES), which synergistically integrates a Multimodal Workbench, an Intelligence Hub, and a modular agent cluster. The Multimodal Workbench fuses heterogeneous sensor data (voltage, current, temperature, acoustic) through a progressive three-level fusion strategy with cross-modal attention and Dempster-Shafer evidence theory. The Intelligence Hub formulates task allocation as a constrained optimization problem, which is relaxed to a differentiable softmax routing mechanism. This enables real-time, load-aware scheduling. A fine-tuned large language model (Qwen3-Omni) provides domain-adaptive diagnostic reasoning through closed-loop reinforcement learning from human feedback. Extensive experiments on real-world charging station data demonstrate that FAES achieves 83.2% diagnostic accuracy under few-shot cross-dataset transfer-a 15.8 percentage point improvement over training from scratch and reduces average response time by 42.9% (from 4.2 s to 2.4 s) via dynamic multi-agent scheduling. Ablation studies quantify the contribution of each component, while hallucination analysis confirms a low rate of just 0.4%. These results establish FAES as an explainable, generalizable solution for industrial fault diagnosis, filling a critical gap in the application of LLM-based multi-agent collaboration to charging station maintenance.

items.title: Research on the Construction of an Early Cancer Warning AI Model Based on Genomic Data and Clinical Phenotypes
items.abstract: The objective of this study is to develop an artificial intelligence model for early cancer warning that integrates genomic data, clinical phenotypic characteristics, and other elements, yielding insights through comprehensive analysis. The aim is to significantly improve the detection rate and accuracy of early cancer symptom screening, address the challenge of early-stage malignancy's concealment, enable identification and feedback on micro lesions, and support clinical diagnosis. This study employs multimodal data fusion techniques to incorporate genomic features such as gene mutations and copy number variations, combined with patient clinical indicators, and utilizes deep learning approaches to establish a dual-channel feature extraction network. Preliminary simulation results demonstrate that the model achieves a sensitivity of 92.3%, specificity of 89.7%, and an AUC value of 0.94 on the independent test set, markedly outperforming traditional single-marker detection methods (P <0.01). Overall, this study provides a novel approach for early cancer screening with significant potential for clinical translation.

items.title: Revisiting Starr (1969)—Social Benefit Versus Technological Risk: What is Our Society Willing to Pay for Safety?
items.abstract: Abstract This contribution examines how societies perceive and manage technological risks, focusing on the ethical and economic dimensions of valuing human life. Technological advancements have historically improved quality of life but have introduced risks requiring trade-offs between safety and cost. Starr’s seminal 1969 study, later corroborated by further research, illustrated that voluntary risks are tolerated at much higher levels than involuntary ones, and that public acceptance of risk depends on perceived benefits. Since Starr’s publication, the popularity of cost-benefit analysis in decision-making has increased exponentially, yet it still struggles to capture key ethical, social, and psychological factors, making purely rational models insufficient. Today, the unanticipated increase in data availability and the development of processing infrastructure might provide opportunities. However, emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence introduce new forms of risk that require careful consideration and open debate. Ultimately, what our society is willing to pay for safety can only be answered through inclusive and adaptive risk governance approaches with safeguards against power imbalance and tunnel vision, fostering public trust and transparent deliberation of values and ethical dilemmas rather than relying solely on numeric thresholds or precedents.

items.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Disease and Pest Management in Cauliflower: A Review
items.abstract: Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis L.) is a nutritionally important cole vegetable and a high-value component of intensive vegetable production. Its yield and market quality are frequently reduced by bacterial, fungal and oomycete diseases and by insect pests that cause direct feeding injury or facilitate secondary infections. Conventional disease and pest surveillance is largely dependent on visual scouting, expert diagnosis and periodic field observations. These approaches remain indispensable, but they can be labour-intensive, subjective and difficult to scale over large production areas. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, image segmentation, object detection, remote sensing and predictive analytics, offers a complementary approach for rapid and repeatable crop-health assessment. This review examines the potential role of AI in cauliflower disease and pest management, covering image acquisition, disease classification, lesion localisation, severity estimation, insect identification, automated counting, forecasting, smartphone applications, UAV-based surveillance and AI-enabled integrated pest management. Cauliflower-specific research has demonstrated promising performance of deep-learning models. The Cauli-Det modified YOLOv8 system reported precision of 93.2%, recall of 82.6% and mean average precision of 91.1% for bacterial soft rot, downy mildew and black rot in its experimental dataset (Uddin et al., 2024). Another recent cauliflower study reported 99.85% classification accuracy using EfficientNet-B3 under its experimental conditions (Malik et al., 2025). Broader plant-disease research also demonstrates strong potential for CNNs and transfer learning (Mohanty et al., 2016; Ferentinos, 2018), while pest-detection research supports automated insect recognition and monitoring (Thenmozhi & Reddy, 2019; Chakrabarty et al., 2026). However, field variability, limited crop-specific datasets, class imbalance, symptom similarity, model explainability, computational requirements and inadequate independent validation remain major constraints. Future research should integrate AI predictions with weather, crop stage, pest abundance, disease severity and economic thresholds so that the technology supports practical, affordable and environmentally responsible IPM in cauliflower.

items.title: Role of Supervised Learning in the Domain of Otology: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Medical imaging and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies are revolutionarily changing the practice of medicine by enabling disease detection at an early stage, precise diagnostic tests, personalised treatment protocols, and, as a result, better patient outcomes. Imaging modalities like Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) are instrumental in providing precise visual descriptions of the human body. The use of AI, particularly with Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML), can significantly enhance scanning and data analysis operations obtained from these imaging modalities. In otolaryngology, ML and DL are essential tools in the management of complex disorders, such as hearing loss, vestibular disorders, and skull base disorders. Supervised ML has demonstrated improved diagnostic sensitivity, enabling clinicians to make accurate diagnoses of different ear conditions, especially in underserved populations with restricted access to specialist services. The present review attempts to provide a concise overview of the historical progress in AI while illustrating the revolutionary influence of ML technology in middle and inner ear imaging. The articles included in the present review have been chosen from the PubMed database. Supervised learning has immense potential to enhance the diagnosis and management of hearing disorders and offers a clear path for future research and clinical application in this critical area.

items.title: SADA: semantic-aware perturbation and dual-view alignment for privacy-preserving LLMs
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted widespread attention owing to their strong capabilities in text comprehension and generation. However, despite their popularity in cloud-based inference services, concerns have emerged regarding the potential leakage of sensitive user information. Existing context perturbation methods with differential privacy apply uniform noise to input tokens to mitigate such risks, facing the trade-off between privacy efficiency and generation quality. To narrow this gap, we propose semantic-aware perturbation and dual-view alignment (SADA) for privacy-preserving LLMs inference. SADA introduces two plug-in modules named the perturbation module and alignment module. In the perturbation module, we design ADRTEXT, a semantic-aware local differential privacy (LDP) mechanism that achieves differentiated protection through token-level sensitivity analysis. Then, a novel dual-view alignment strategy is introduced in the alignment module to bridge a randomized perturbed view with an entity-free semantic skeleton, optimizing the trade-off between LDP-induced noise and generation quality. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that SADA achieves effective privacy protection while maintaining a higher generation quality.

items.title: SAGE-AIP: A Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for Predicting AI Adoption and Productivity Across Multiple Data Scales
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is frequently associated with productivity improvement, yet empirical conclusions depend on where AI exposure is measured, how productivity is defined, and which model is used. This study develops a multi-scale comparative framework using three datasets: 145,000 AI-adoption records from 10 countries and eight industries; 2,074 observed country-year records from 233 country or regional units (2015–2023); and 150 employee-level observations. Robust regression, country fixed effects, dynamic fixed effects, and difference-GMM sensitivity analysis are combined with a proposed Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for AI Adoption and Productivity (SAGE-AIP), which is benchmarked against six established regressors using temporal holdouts for the two longitudinal datasets and a train–test split for the employee data. The adoption dataset shows almost no systematic structure (R2 = 0.00018), and SAGE-AIP does not improve on simpler models there (test RMSE 28.976 vs. 28.900 for Elastic Net). In the global panel, automation intensity is strongly associated with AI-attributed productivity (β = 19.882, SE = 0.434), and SAGE-AIP attains the lowest test RMSE (4.448; R2 = 0.544). At the employee level, recorded AI-tool information remains positively associated with productivity (β = 0.905, SE = 0.220), but Random Forest outperforms SAGE-AIP (test RMSE 0.435 vs. 0.583). SAGE-AIP is therefore not uniformly superior; its value is scale-specific, which supports evaluating models across data scales rather than relying on a single dataset or model class.

items.title: Scalable Gemini-Based Code Review System: An Asynchronous Microservices Architecture for Learning Analytics
items.abstract: Manual inspection of students' GitHub commit histories to assess their programming activity presents significant scalability challenges when handling numerous repositories across a semester. This research developed and evaluated an AI-based commit analysis system that uses the Gemini language model to generate natural-language summaries of student programming activity, intended to support lecturers' review of GitHub-based coursework. The system was implemented using a prototyping methodology with an asynchronous, containerized architecture comprising a Vue.js front-end, a Laravel back-end, a PostgreSQL database, and a Redis-based job queue deployed in separate Docker containers. To keep the user-facing application responsive, AI analysis is processed asynchronously through a provider-abstraction layer accessing Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite via OpenRouter, decoupling user interactions from computationally intensive model inference. System performance was evaluated using Apache JMeter on a 2-vCPU, 4-GB-RAM server, following the Performance Efficiency and Reliability characteristics of ISO/IEC 25010:2023. The back-end demonstrated a 0% error rate across 4,625 GitHub Feature requests. However, mean response time increased from 346.0 ms (10 users) to 6,743.8 ms (100 users), with throughput plateauing beyond 25 concurrent users, indicating a practical capacity threshold of 25–50 concurrent users. The AI Feedback path achieved a 100% success rate with a synchronous request-dispatch latency of 2.5–3.8 s across 90 requests; these are user-facing dispatch latencies and exclude LLM inference time. These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of the proposed asynchronous architecture for AI-assisted commit analysis at a moderate classroom scale; they do not constitute an evaluation of the accuracy, pedagogical usefulness, or learning-outcome impact of the generated feedback, which remain directions for future work. The primary limitation observed is performance degradation under high concurrency, which will require caching, database connection pooling, and vertical scaling for broader institutional deployment

items.title: Sensor Imaging Systems: Advancements, Applications, and Emerging Techniques
items.abstract: In the last decade, significant progress and notable achievements in machine learning (ML) technologies have enabled the collection, analysis, and interpretation of an unprecedented volume of sensory data. A paradigm shift is occurring in the field of sensor systems, where smart sensor systems are revolutionizing the traditional methods of comprehending the world. Smart sensor systems utilize both traditional and emerging artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, as well as advanced computer hardware, to develop complex methods that are specifically designed for sensing applications. These models are capable of integrating various sensing methods to gain a comprehensive understanding of the monitored system. This chapter presents a comprehensive evaluation of the latest sensing applications that use ML-enabled sensor models. The discussion focuses on the first implementation of well-recognized ML techniques in sensor models for real-time applications. The next sections provide an overview of the practical applications of sensing technology. This study describes how sensor technologies are integrated with ML models to create intelligent models and how these systems provide real-time advantages. Ultimately, this chapter offers an analysis of the present opportunities and obstacles 2 that future intelligent sensing systems may face, as well as the potential chances that may arise.

items.title: Serum uric acid and estimated glomerular filtration rate in working-age males: a 10-year longitudinal study of annual health check-up data from an occupational cohort in Japan
items.abstract: Abstract Background Maintaining kidney health before the onset of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an important goal in nephrology and preventive medicine. Serum uric acid (SUA) levels have been associated with kidney dysfunction; however, evidence from long-term repeated-measures studies in working-age cohorts undergoing routine health check-ups remains limited. This study aimed to examine the longitudinal association between time-varying SUA levels and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) across the 10-year follow-up using annual health check-up data from an occupational cohort in Japan. Methods A retrospective longitudinal study was conducted using annual health check-up data from 5403 working-age males in an occupational cohort in the Kansai region of Japan, composed primarily of manufacturing-sector employees. The primary complete-case analysis included 56,816 observations from 5402 participants. eGFR was calculated at each annual health check-up. The longitudinal association between time-varying SUA and concurrently assessed eGFR was examined using linear mixed-effects models that included participant-specific random intercepts and participant-specific random slopes for measurement wave and SUA. The primary model was adjusted for demographic, clinical, and lifestyle factors as time-varying covariates. Sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and alternative exposure and outcome measures. Results At baseline, the mean age was 46.5 years, the mean SUA level was 6.1 mg/dL, and the mean eGFR was 79.1 mL/min/1.73 m². Over the 10-year follow-up period, the mean eGFR declined to 70.1 mL/min/1.73 m², whereas the mean SUA level changed from 6.1 to 6.2 mg/dL. In the primary model, each 1 mg/dL higher SUA level was associated with a 3.25 mL/min/1.73 m² lower eGFR (95% confidence interval, − 3.34 to − 3.16; p < 0.001). These findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Conclusions In this occupational cohort of working-age males, a higher SUA level was longitudinally associated with lower eGFR. These findings suggest that SUA may provide additional information for interpreting eGFR levels and their longitudinal changes in health check-up settings. Further studies are warranted to determine its utility as an epidemiological marker in kidney function assessment in occupational health settings. Trial registration Not applicable.

items.title: Shadow AI usage and ethical AI adoption: the moderating role of chief AI officer governance
items.abstract: Purpose The rapid emergence of Shadow artificial intelligence (AI), the informal and unauthorised use of AI tools by employees, poses a growing challenge for global organisations. It creates cybersecurity threats, compliance risks, data breaches and ethical violations such as bias and opacity, ultimately undermining ethical AI adoption and stakeholder trust. Existing research often portrays the Chief AI Officer (CAIO) as a static role, focusing on compliance enforcement or policy integration while overlooking its potential to balance innovation and governance. This study aims to examine how the CAIO as a moderator influences the relationship between Shadow AI Usage and Ethical AI Adoption. Design/methodology/approach A deductive, theory-driven, cross-sectional research design was adopted, drawing on 665 AI practitioners and organisational decision-makers recruited through professional networks across multiple countries. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was employed to test the hypothesised moderating relationship. Findings Higher Shadow AI Usage was negatively associated with Ethical AI Adoption, whereas the positive Shadow AI Usage × CAIO interaction indicates that stronger CAIO governance attenuates this negative relationship. Originality/value This study contributes to AI governance research by conceptualising CAIO governance as an organisational boundary condition that attenuates the negative association between Shadow AI Usage and Ethical AI Adoption.
