items.abstract: The Metacognitive Creative Destruction (MCD) model approaches educational innovation as a perpetual spiral process. Contradiction (accumulated cognitive conflicts that resist interpretation), activates Metacognitive Capacity, enabling Destructive Unlearning Propensity, the conscious abandonment of outdated mental schemas, which in turn enables Creative Reconstruction Ability, and ultimately, new knowledge. In the model’s empirical validation with 1,498 teachers, a critical finding emerged: AI Augmentation Intensity (AIA) predicted Metacognitive Capacity (MC) and Creative Reconstruction Ability (CRA), but not Destructive Unlearning Propensity (DUP).This article argues that this finding is not accidental, but reflects an inherent weakness of modern AI systems, and more specifically, the tendency toward AI Sycophancy. Models trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) tend to avoid disagreements and be likable to the user, preventing the individual from experiencing cognitive conflicts, perpetuating their already formed beliefs at the expense of scientific accuracy.Therefore, in an environment of “algorithmic flattery”, the necessary contradictions that trigger unlearning are not produced. Based on the MCD model, it is concluded that the absence of unlearning, that is, the deliberate and conscious abandonment of outdated beliefs, mental models and practices, makes the reconstruction of knowledge absolutely superficial and thus, algorithmically condescending interaction does not produce deep and authentic knowledge, regardless of AI Augmentation Intensity.

items.title: THE PARTICLE THAT KEPT MOVING: A SWARM-EQUATION BIOGRAPHY OF SATISH GAJAWADA (IIT ROORKEE ALUMNUS). INERTIA, MEMORY, GUIDANCE AND WONDER IN FOURTEEN YEARS OF INDEPENDENT ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH
items.abstract: Most biographies follow a life through time. This one follows a life through an equation. Satish Gajawada, an Integrated Dual Degree (B.Tech + M.Tech) graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (2012), has spent fourteen years as an independent researcher who gives names, structure and heart to ideas in artificial intelligence: Excellent AI (EAI), Very Highly Advanced AI (VHAAI), Out of the Box AI (OBAI), a society (ISVHAAI), a family of value-themed swarm algorithms, thirteen theories of human purpose, a 108-right taxonomy of human rights, and a lifelong “thesis” supervised by his parents and GOD. Reading the particle swarm update rule as a metaphor for a research life, this article identifies four forces (inertia, personal best, global best and exploration) and one outcome: a position update that, in 2026, turned decisively toward testing and open disclosure. Drawing on eight source documents, with each statement attributed to a published work, a manuscript or the subject’s own account, we show that a reproducible genetic-algorithm and PSO experiment found a fairness weight that cut a demographic-parity gap from 0.121 to 0.016 for 1.9 points of accuracy, and a gentler weight that improved accuracy and fairness together. Itemised output rose from one entry in 2012 to twelve in 2026. We conclude that Gajawada is a builder of human-centred vocabulary and institutions, a grateful son, a joyful experimenter and a candid author, and that his life offers every learner a portable update rule: keep your direction, honour your best, listen to your guides, stay curious, and keep moving.

items.title: THE ROLE OF AI-POWERED DUOLINGO AND ELSA SPEAK APPS IN REDUCING SPEAKING ANXIETY AMONG ENGLISH LEARNERS IN PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES OF DHAKA, BANGLADESH
items.abstract: This study has explored the influence of speaking anxiety as a major obstacle for English as foreign language learners (EFL) in their non-native environment like in the private universities in Dhaka, Bangladesh. With the up rise of Artificial Intelligence, English language learning applications have incorporated AI-based features to enhance the learning experience. This finding examined how AI-supported speaking apps, in this instance, Duolingo and ELSA Speak, reduce speaking anxiety and increase learners' confidence, fluency and speaking skills through AI-driven personalized feedback, gamified interaction and adaptive learning. This research used mixed-method approach, which included qualitative and quantitative methods to provide comprehensive insights and understanding. The results of the study pointed to the effectiveness of AI-based language learning apps in creating a supportive language-learning atmosphere, enhancing the learning process and reducing stress levels when practicing oral communication. The results of this study could contribute to the understanding of how AI-based app-based learning can be incorporated in the university curriculum and evidence-based recommendations for teachers, educational technology designers and policy makers.

items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNING: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND PEDAGOGICAL IMPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing Englishlanguage learning by providing personalized instruction, immediate feedback,interactive communication, and opportunities for independent practice. This paperexamines the potential benefits and challenges of integrating AI technologies intoEnglish as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning. The study adopts a literature reviewapproach and draws on existing empirical research, systematic reviews, andinternational educational guidance. The reviewed literature suggests that AI-supportedlearning can contribute to language development, particularly by providing writingfeedback, facilitating conversational practice, and supporting learner engagement.However, the effectiveness of these technologies depends on the quality of AIgenerated feedback, learners’ digital literacy, appropriate pedagogical guidance, andresponsible use. Potential challenges include inaccurate information, excessivedependence on AI, academic integrity concerns, and data privacy risks. The paperargues that AI should complement rather than replace teachers and meaningful humaninteraction. It concludes that the responsible integration of AI into English languageeducation requires clear learning objectives, critical evaluation of AI-generated content,and a balanced combination of technological tools and teacher-led instruction.
